# Introduction
```{python}
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

sns.set_context('talk')

df = sns.load_dataset('iris')

```

 Using the iris dataset from seaborn. We have data from 
 `{python} f"{df.shape[0]}"` flowers.
 Our research question is to study whether the petal width correlates with petal length. 

 

# Literature Review

We will come back to the LR. 

# Method

Given that we have two columns of continous data (length of petal and width of petal measured in millimeters) we will evaluate this relationship using simple correlation analysis and also a scatterplot. These two methods are classic and traditional starting points while evaluating data like these. 

# Results  

```{python}
corr_val = np.array(df[['petal_length', 'petal_width']].corr())[0][1]

narrative = "a very strong negative correlation"

if corr_val > .8:
  narrative = "a very strong positive correlation"
elif corr_val > .4:
  narrative = "a moderate positive correlation"
elif corr_val > 0:
  narrative = "a positive but weak correlation"
elif corr_val > -.4:
  narrative = "a moderate negative correlation"



```
Using the class simple Pearson correlation approach these data produce a correlation coefficient of  `{python} f"{corr_val: .5f}"`; given this result we conclude that the realtionship is `{python} f"{narrative}"`.

```{python}
#| label: fig-length-width-scatter
#| fig-cap: A scatterplot of petal length and width 

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.5))

sns.scatterplot(data=df, y='petal_length', x='petal_width')

plt.ylabel('Petal width (mm)')
plt.xlabel('Petal length (mm)')
```
As shown in @fig-length-width-scatter we see additional evidence of `{python} f"{narrative}"` between an iris flower petal length and petal width. 

# Discussion

Now that this long standing problem of over 10 minutes is resolved thanks to the deligient efforts of UW-Madison's DSHB program, science has once again triumped in establishing that the relationship that there is a positivly correlated relationship between iris petal width and iris petal length as a matter of imperically certain ground truth. 

```{python}

sns.lmplot(data=df, x='petal_length' , y='petal_width')

sns.jointplot(x = df['petal_length'], y = df['petal_width'])

sns.jointplot(x = df['petal_length'], y = df['petal_width'], kind= 'hex', color = "red")
```
